title: 🌍 Venezuela Demands Lifting the Ban on ChatGPT, Claude, and Copilot... and Its Citizens Are Cut Off From AI!
body: 🌍 Venezuela Demands Lifting the Ban on ChatGPT, Claude, and Copilot... and Its Citizens Are Cut Off From AI!

On November 20, Venezuela's interim president, Delcy Rodríguez, tasked her foreign minister, Oliver Blanco, with taking urgent diplomatic steps to demand that global AI platforms lift the restrictions that prevent Venezuelans from reaching them.

Users in Venezuela currently cannot directly access the most famous AI platforms, such as ChatGPT, Microsoft's Copilot, and Claude, and instead see a message saying the service is unavailable, while some platforms work only through a virtual private network.

Rodríguez said, in a meeting with entrepreneurs, that removing these barriers aims to make it easier for the new generation to reach modern technologies, develop their skills, and grow their creativity, noting that the restrictions on global tech platforms are often linked to foreign sanctions and regulations, led by American sanctions.
Venezuela announced in September 2025 plans to develop its own local AI platform and to introduce teaching of this technology in schools, without setting a date for its launch.
Simply put: millions of people in Venezuela are cut off from the most famous AI tools because of sanctions; so can technology stay neutral when politics intervenes?
